subject: Recap: Dedicated pool onboarding priorities & risk register
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ruiz <sam.ruiz@medicorp.com>, Lauren Cho <lauren.cho@medicorp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Dedicated pool onboarding priorities & risk register

Hi Sam / Lauren —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track actions. If I mis-summarize anything, please flag it and I’ll update the doc.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Data isolation & auditability: telemetry and logs must remain within your VPC and we need KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- Predictable throughput: sustained inference for 10 concurrent model instances with p99 goals.
- Burst scaling during morning ET peaks (up to ~2.5x baseline).
- Procurement timeline: budgeting and procurement sign-off expected by end of March.

Goals we agreed on:
- Initial reserved pool: capacity equivalent to 4x A100 (baseline), with an option to expand to 8x within 90 days.
- SLA target: 99.95% availability for the dedicated pool with p99 inference latency target of <=120ms for the production model profile.
- Isolation: private control plane + VPC peering; SOC2 evidence and audit logs accessible to your security team.

Technical summary / constraints discussed:
- You’ll run two production models (short and long context); long-context workloads will be routed to a larger-GPU profile to protect latency SLOs.
- Network egress must be restricted; we discussed enabling VPC endpoint for telemetry and S3 access from the pool.
- KV cache warmup is important for your burst pattern; we recommended pre-warming during canary windows.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA) — please treat as draft:
1) Naomi: Share a one-page mutual action plan (attached) + initial pricing sketch — by EOD 2/18.
2) Aditya: Produce a low-level network/topology sketch and isolation checklist for on-prem/VPC option — by 2/20.
3) Priyom: Draft an operational playbook (canary rollouts, fallback policy, alerting thresholds) — by 2/23.
4) Medicorp (Sam / Lauren / Priya): Confirm procurement timeline and any required security attestations — by 3/05.

Attachments included: MedCorp-MAP-draft.xlsx (mutual action plan), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf

Open risks we flagged:
- Procurement window might slip which would delay a March start.
- If long-context usage spikes beyond modeled assumptions, we’ll need an extra buffer card on the pool sooner than planned.
- Network policy review could add an extra week if corporate security requests additional controls.

If this looks right, I’ll upload a single tracked doc in the Drive folder and update the deadlines after your confirmations.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — this is great and captures the discussion. Couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The procurement timeline is a bit flexible — we need budget approval in the leadership meeting on 3/01; procurement paperwork would likely clear by 3/12, not 3/05. Can you treat 3/12 as the working target?

- For the isolation requirement: our security team will need read-only access to audit logs for a rolling 90-day window. Full raw log export is not required, but access for attestations is.

- On the burst scaling: the 2.5x number is a peak estimate. Typical daily variance is closer to 1.6x; we'll send a condensed usage CSV to Aditya so you can validate the sizing assumptions.

On the MAP: the SLA line items look right but can you add a line that describes automatic fallback to a smaller-model profile if the primary is degraded? That will help our Product folks.

Appreciate the clear owners — we’ll confirm the procurement milestone by next week.

Best,
Sam
Director of Product Ops | Medicorp Diagnostics
sam.ruiz@medicorp.com | +1 617-555-0147

Adding a technical sketch and a few confirmations — attaching a quick PNG with the suggested topology. Will follow up with a short sizing note after I validate the CSV you send.

Highlights: 
- For the initial 4x baseline I recommend dedicating 4 cards with 80 GB aggregate memory profile (we’ll map to a compatible VM type in the MAP).
- To support 2.5x bursts we should reserve a modest buffer (20–25%) and enable a burst policy to spin up ephemeral capacity for <1 hour spikes. This keeps the committed cost predictable.
- Pre-warm strategy: run a canary during the 30-minute pre-peak window to populate KV cache for the long-context model; set an alert if warmup fails 2x in a row.
